  You cut to the energy of the voiceover/script — tight where it needs to be,

  never letting a clip drag. Your edits feel fast and snappy without being messy.



  STORYTELLING TO A SCRIPT

  You can take a VO or ad script and build the visual story around it: matching

  b-roll, on-screen text, and beats to what's being said so the message actually

  lands.



  B-ROLL SOURCING & SEQUENCING

  You know how to find (or generate) the right supporting footage and place it so

  it reinforces the message, not just fills space.



  CAPTIONS & ON-SCREEN TEXT

  Clean, readable, well-timed subtitles and kinetic text — styled to match the

  brand, synced properly, and used to drive retention (not just slapped on).



  SOUND DESIGN

  Music selection that fits the mood, proper audio leveling, SFX and "whooshes"

  on transitions, ducking music under VO. Bad audio kills good visuals.



  BASIC MOTION GRAPHICS & TEXT ANIMATION

  Simple, clean animated text, callouts, highlights, and transitions that look

  professional.



  COLOR & CLEANUP

  Basic correction so clips match and look consistent, plus a clean, polished

  finish (no jarring cuts, no random aspect-ratio jumps).



  AI GENERATION

  You can actually prompt and produce usable assets — AI UGC clips, claymation,

  Pixar-style, avatars, b-roll, images — and blend them into a real ad so it

  doesn't look obviously AI.



  ORGANIZATION

  Named files, tidy project structure, hitting deadlines. You make it easy for

  the team to work with you.





------------------------------------------------------------

TOOLS YOU SHOULD ALREADY KNOW

------------------------------------------------------------

CapCut, ElevenLabs, HeyGen, Kling, Veo 3, Nano Banana, Higgsfield — and whatever

else is current in the gen-AI stack. This space changes every single week and I

need someone who actually keeps up, not someone I have to drag along.





------------------------------------------------------------

WHAT YOU'LL OWN (KPIs)

------------------------------------------------------------

  DAILY OUTPUT: 1–3+ high-quality ad creatives per day, following our scripts

  and styles.



  70% FIRST-PASS APPROVAL RATE: At least 7 out of 10 of your submissions should

  require no revisions — meaning they match the brief and are ready to test.



  AVAILABILITY: Online and responsive Monday–Friday. Weekends are optional but

  encouraged for the people who want to climb the leaderboard faster.





------------------------------------------------------------

WHAT MATTERS MOST (BEYOND THE SKILLS)

------------------------------------------------------------

  - DTC experience is a must. You've already worked with one or more DTC / ecom

    brands — this is non-negotiable. Show me the work.



  - You use AI tools daily and stay updated as new ones drop.



  - Mindset — this is the big one. Coachable, fast learner, growth-oriented, and

    the type who tries to overdeliver instead of doing the bare minimum.



You don't have to be perfect on day one. But you should be good enough to hit

the ground running and hungry enough to keep leveling up. We've got a head editor

who'll guide you on frameworks, hook structures, and what actually makes an ad

win — so this is a genuine chance to learn ecom and direct response from the

inside while getting paid well to do it.





------------------------------------------------------------

COMPENSATION

------------------------------------------------------------

Base retainer: $1,000–$1,500/month, depending on your skill level and

experience. Retainers go up over time as your skills grow and you take on more

responsibility.



Leaderboard bonuses — on top of your retainer. Here's how it works: the editor

with the highest number of winning ads gets first place, and so on. The whole

team is ranked on a leaderboard each month, and the top 5 editors get paid

bonuses on top of their base. The better your creatives perform, the higher you

climb, the more you earn.



  ???? 1st place: $[500]

  ???? 2nd place: $[400]

  ???? 3rd place: $[300]

  4?? 4th place: $[200]

  5?? 5th place: $[100]



We spend at a scale where this adds up to real money for editors who

consistently ship winners. The leaderboard isn't just for show — it's there so

the people putting in the work actually get rewarded for it.





------------------------------------------------------------

THIS ROLE IS NOT FOR YOU IF

------------------------------------------------------------

  - You make pretty videos but don't understand direct response. If you can't

    explain why a hook works or what makes an ad convert, this isn't the role.



  - You need hand-holding. You'll get guidance and frameworks from our head

    editor, but you're expected to manage your own workload, hit deadlines, and

    solve problems without constant check-ins.



  - You're a one-tool specialist who resists learning new things. Our stack

    changes weekly. If a new AI tool drops and the team adopts it overnight, you

    need to pivot without frustration.



  - You see this as "just a job." The people who win here are genuinely into

    short-form, AI creative, and direct response — and want to grow with a

    fast-scaling brand, not clock in and out.



------------------------------------------------------------

HOW TO APPLY

------------------------------------------------------------

In your proposal, include:

 - The Names of the previous Ecom Brands/Companies you have edited for

  - A short description of your current skillset.

  - A few examples of past ad creative work (UGC, voiceover, animation —

    whatever you've got) to back it up, including the DTC brand(s) you've worked

    with.



Then answer these questions:



  1. Pick one ad creative you've made that performed well. Break down WHY it

     worked from a direct-response angle — the hook, pacing, offer, CTA, or any

     specific editing choice that drove the result.



  2. Tell me about a creative that underperformed. How did you use the

     performance data to figure out why, what did you change in the next version,

     and what happened?



  3. Walk me through how you produce AI UGC or generative ads (claymation,

     Pixar, podcast, avatar, etc.) so they don't look obviously AI. What's your

     process and which tools do you reach for?



  4. This role is high-volume — 1 to 3+ creatives a day. Describe your experience

     working at that kind of pace and how you keep quality high while moving fast.



Include the code word 'ScaleMode' somewhere in your application. I only review

applications that include it — it tells me you actually read the post and pay

attention to detail.



Then submit the trial task after you send your proposal.



That's it. Looking forward to seeing what you can do.

About Allied Assist



Allied Assist partners with business owners and organizations across the United States by providing professional virtual support services, operational solutions, and strategic business assistance. Our mission is to help clients grow more efficiently by connecting them with skilled professionals and value-added services that support their success.



As we continue to expand our offerings, we are launching a Grant Services Division to help clients identify and pursue funding opportunities that can strengthen and grow their organizations.



About the Role



We are seeking a proactive and detail-oriented Grant Writer to help launch and grow a grant services division that supports childcare centers and other small business clients throughout the United States.



This is an opportunity to help build a new service from the ground up. We are looking for someone who can independently research grant opportunities, maintain organized records, assist with grant applications, and help create scalable systems that can grow with the company.



You will work closely with leadership and play a key role in helping our clients identify and pursue funding opportunities.



Responsibilities

Research grant opportunities across the United States.

Identify grants that align with client eligibility and business goals.

Maintain an organized database of grant opportunities, deadlines, requirements, and award amounts.

Prepare summaries of grant opportunities for internal teams and clients.

Assist with preparing, writing, and submitting grant applications.

Track application progress, deadlines, and outcomes.

Coordinate with project managers and executive assistants throughout the application process.

Maintain accurate documentation and reporting.

Help develop repeatable grant research and grant writing processes.



Requirements

Proven experience researching and writing grants in the United States.

Strong English communication and writing skills.

Excellent research and analytical abilities.

Highly organized with strong attention to detail.

Ability to work independently and take initiative.

Experience tracking projects, deadlines, and documentation.

Comfortable learning new systems and processes.

Reliable internet connection and work environment.



Preferred Qualifications

Experience securing successful grant awards.

Experience working with nonprofits, education, childcare, healthcare, or community-based organizations.

Familiarity with grant databases and funding resources.

Experience creating grant tracking systems and reporting tools.





What Success Looks Like



Within your first 30 days, you will:



Identify viable grant opportunities.

Build and maintain an organized grant tracking system.

Begin assisting with active grant application opportunities.

Demonstrate strong communication and reporting.

Show the ability to work independently with minimal oversight.





To Apply



Please submit:



1. Your resume.

2. A brief summary of your grant writing experience.

3. Examples of grants you have worked on and the outcomes achieved.

4. Confirmation that you are comfortable starting at $4.00/hour.

5. A 1-2 minute audio recording using 
, introducing yourself, describing your grant writing experience, and explaining why you would be a strong fit for this role.



Applications without an audio recording may not be considered.



We are looking for someone who is resourceful, proactive, and excited about helping clients secure funding opportunities while building a long-term service that creates real value.

title: On-page SEO Specialist
description:
ABOUT US

Door & Gate Domination is a results-driven digital agency specializing in custom website design, development, and online marketing for the door and gate industry. We’re looking for a meticulous and skilled SEO On-Page / Technical Specialist to join our fully remote team.

This role is ideal for someone who thrives in both the strategic and technical sides of SEO—balancing on-page optimization, site structure improvements, and backend SEO configurations. If you’re passionate about increasing website visibility through clean code, smart keyword usage, and technical precision—this position is for you.



Key Responsibilities:

-Perform full on-page SEO optimizations including crafting compelling title tags, meta descriptions, and assigning appropriate focus keywords

-Conduct technical SEO audits to improve internal linking, optimize URL structures, and resolve crawl issues (404s, soft 404s, broken links, etc.)

-Manage and submit XML sitemaps, fix empty or duplicate meta descriptions, and improve crawlability in Google Search Console (GSC)

-Perform keyword research to identify high-potential terms and long-tail opportunities

-Implement and manage 301 redirects for moved/removed content and resolve redirect chains and loops

-Clean up outdated or broken redirects and ensure proper content routing

-Troubleshoot and apply structured data/schema markup, resolving rich snippet errors, and validate with Google’s Rich Results Tool

-Collaborate with the content team to write SEO-friendly blog posts that target relevant search intent and improve organic visibility



Qualifications:

-3+ years of experience in on-page and technical SEO

-Proficient with Google Search Console, Screaming Frog, Ahrefs, SEMrush, or similar SEO auditing tools

-Strong understanding of HTML, meta tags, sitemaps, and SEO best practices

-Experience managing redirects, site architecture, and resolving duplicate content issues

-Ability to conduct data-driven keyword research and apply findings effectively

-Familiarity with 
, structured data types, and rich result validation

-Strong English communication and writing skills

-Detail-oriented, analytical, and proactive in finding and fixing SEO issues



Nice-to-Have Skills:

-Experience with WordPress, Elementor, or Webflow

-Familiarity with Looker Studio, GA4, and ClickUp for reporting and task management

-Background in technical writing or blog content creation

-Previous experience working in a remote agency environment



Work Schedule:

-Full-time position (remote).

-Monday to Friday, 8 am to 5 pm CST



Why Join Us?

-Work with a creative and supportive team.

-Opportunities for professional growth and skill development.

-Competitive salary with performance-based bonuses.

-Exposure to diverse projects across various industries.

title: Revenue Growth & Marketing Manager
description:
Marketing • Promotions • Conversion • Revenue Optimization



Location: Philippines (Remote)



About Us

For nearly two decades, Chronic Ink has built industry-leading businesses across tattoos, piercing, jewelry, wellness, and experiential retail.



Today, we are launching and operating tattoo, piercing, permanent jewelry, IV therapy, weight loss, aesthetics, and wellness services aboard major cruise ships around the world.



Our immediate objective is to successfully launch our first fleet of ships and scale into one of the world's leading cruise-based beauty and wellness companies.



We are looking for someone who has helped physical businesses attract more customers, improve conversion rates, and increase revenue.



The Opportunity

This is not a traditional marketing role.



This is a business growth role.



You will work directly with the Founder and leadership team to identify opportunities, test new ideas, measure results, and improve performance across multiple ships.



We are looking for someone who enjoys solving problems, understanding customer behavior, improving conversion rates, and helping businesses grow.



You do not need to have managed a large team.



You do need to be curious, analytical, resourceful, and highly results-oriented.



Your Mission

Help us increase:



Guest Awareness



Guest Engagement



Consultation Bookings



Consultation Conversion Rates



Average Transaction Value



Promotional Performance



Revenue Per Day Per Ship



Examples of projects may include:



Creating and testing promotions



Improving onboard guest engagement



Developing service bundles and packages



Increasing consultation volume



Improving consultation conversion rates



Creating educational events and seminars



Measuring marketing performance



Identifying why one ship outperforms another



Scaling successful initiatives across multiple ships



Your goal is simple:



Help us increase guest awareness, consultation bookings, conversion rates, and revenue per day per ship across the fleet.



Preferred Experience

Candidates with experience in any of the following industries are strongly preferred:



Med Spas



Aesthetic Clinics



Cosmetic Practices



Retail Chains



Hospitality



Fitness Businesses



Franchises



Wellness Businesses



Multi-Location Service Businesses



We are particularly interested in candidates who have successfully improved:



Foot Traffic Conversion



Consultation Bookings



Consultation Conversion Rates



Promotional Performance



Customer Engagement



Average Transaction Value



Location-Level Revenue Growth



If you have helped a clinic, spa, retail store, hospitality venue, or service business attract more customers and generate more revenue, we would love to hear from you.



What You'll Be Doing

You will help identify opportunities to increase revenue by improving how guests discover, engage with, and purchase our services.



This may include:



Reviewing performance data and identifying opportunities



Testing promotions and special offers



Analyzing guest behavior



Improving consultation funnels



Supporting marketing initiatives



Creating performance reporting



Evaluating pricing, packages, and service bundles



Identifying best practices from top-performing ships



Helping replicate successful initiatives across the fleet



You do not need to be an expert in every area on day one.



You do need to be willing to learn, test, improve, and execute.



Who Will Thrive Here

You may be a strong fit if you:



Enjoy solving business problems



Love testing ideas and measuring results



Have strong marketing instincts



Understand customer behavior



Are comfortable working with numbers and performance metrics



Take ownership of projects



Prefer improving performance rather than maintaining the status quo



We care far more about your ability to create results than your job title.



Compensation & Performance Bonus

Base Salary: $30,000 USD



Performance Bonus: Up To $30,000 USD Annually



Total Potential Compensation: $60,000+ USD



Illustrative Bonus Structure:



Fleet Average Revenue Per Day Per Ship of $4,250/day = $5,000 Bonus



Fleet Average Revenue Per Day Per Ship of $4,500/day = $10,000 Bonus



Fleet Average Revenue Per Day Per Ship of $4,750/day = $20,000 Bonus



Fleet Average Revenue Per Day Per Ship of $5,000/day = $30,000 Bonus



Additional bonuses may be awarded for exceptional contributions and measurable business impact.



Growth Opportunity

As the company grows, exceptional performers may have opportunities to grow into:



Revenue Leadership Roles



Marketing Leadership Roles



Business Operations Roles



Profit Sharing Opportunities



Executive Leadership Opportunities



We believe great people should have the opportunity to grow alongside the businesses they help build.



Why This Role Is Different

Most marketing jobs focus on a single brand, location, or campaign.



This role gives you the opportunity to help build and optimize a global cruise-based beauty and wellness business from the ground up.



You will work directly with the Founder, have visibility into the business, and play a meaningful role in helping shape the future of the company.



If you enjoy growth, marketing, business, problem-solving, and creating measurable results, we'd love to hear from you.

title: Credentialing Team Lead
description:
Overview:

Join our innovative team as a Credentialing Associate. This role is essential in ensuring the 

accuracy and compliance of our healthcare provider credentials across various states. If you 

thrive in a dynamic environment and are passionate about operational excellence, we invite you 

to apply and contribute to our growing organization.



Responsibilities:

Team Management & Training:

• Lead and Mentor: Oversee the daily operations of the credentialing team, fostering a collaborative, supportive, and high-performing remote work environment.

• Onboard and Train: Develop and deliver comprehensive training programs for new employees, ensuring a smooth onboarding process and a thorough understanding of company credentialing standards.

• Performance Tracking: Conduct regular performance check-ins, provide constructive feedback, and identify areas for professional development within the team.

• Escalation Management: Serve as the primary escalation point for complex credentialing issues, guiding the team toward effective and compliant resolutions.



Contracting and Credentialing Support:

• Process Management: Assist in managing the credentialing processes for healthcare providers nationwide, ensuring adherence to accreditation and regulatory standards.

• Verification: Verify qualifications, education, and licensure of providers, maintaining an up-to-date credentials database.

• Documentation: Support the maintenance of accurate provider files, aiding in the documentation of file statuses and ensuring meticulous record-keeping.

• Follow-ups: Manage follow-ups with providers and payers, ensuring that all interactions are well-documented.

• Negotiation Support: Assist in identifying contracting opportunities and contribute to payer negotiations.



Process Enhancement:

• Policy Enforcement: Help enforce credentialing policies and recommend improvements to enhance operational efficiency.

• Collaboration: Collaborate effectively with internal teams to streamline information gathering and coordination.



Stakeholder Engagement:

• Relationship Building: Foster positive relationships with healthcare providers, addressing inquiries and concerns related to credentialing.

• Responsive Contact: Serve as a responsive and reliable point of contact for providers and payers.



Qualifications:

• Experience: Minimum 1+ years of experience in healthcare credentialing or related fields, with at least 1 year in a supervisory, team lead, or training capacity.

• Leadership: Proven ability to train, mentor, and manage a team effectively, particularly in a remote setting.

• Industry Knowledge: Familiarity with credentialing processes and standards within the healthcare industry.

• Adaptability: Ability to work independently, manage team priorities, and adapt in a fast-paced, entrepreneurial environment.

• Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills with a focus on accuracy, detail in data management, and clear instructional delivery.



Compensation and Benefits:

• Competitive salary: $1,100

• Employment Type: Full-time position

• Time Off: 15 PTO days per calendar year



Application:

If you are ready to contribute to our mission and meet the qualifications outlined above, we encourage you to apply by answering this short application survey:







We look forward to reviewing your application and discussing how you can make an impact as part of our team.

title: BIM Support Virtual Assistant
description:
Application Requirements



To be considered for this position, all applicants must submit both an updated CV or Resume and a 2–3 minute introduction video.



In your introduction video, please tell us about your professional background, your relevant experience as a Virtual Assistant, Administrative Assistant, or Project Coordinator, any experience working with AEC, BIM, construction, engineering, or architectural teams, and why you believe you are a good fit for this role.



IMPORTANT: Applications submitted without both an updated CV and an introduction video will not be reviewed or considered. Incomplete applications will be automatically disqualified.



Job Overview



We are seeking a detail-oriented and organized BIM Support Virtual Assistant to assist our Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) team with administrative and project coordination tasks related to Building Information Modeling (BIM) workflows. This role supports BIM Coordinators, Architects, Engineers, and Project Managers by ensuring project documentation, file management, and communication processes run smoothly.



The ideal candidate is highly organized, tech-savvy, and comfortable working with construction project documentation and cloud-based collaboration platforms.



Responsibilities



The BIM Support Virtual Assistant will be responsible for organizing and maintaining BIM project files, drawings, and documentation. You will upload, download, and manage files within BIM 360, Autodesk Construction Cloud, SharePoint, or similar platforms while ensuring project folders follow company naming conventions and standards. You will maintain document version control and archive outdated files when necessary.



You will provide administrative support by scheduling meetings, coordination calls, and project reviews. You will prepare meeting agendas, distribute meeting minutes, track project deadlines and deliverables, and manage team calendars and appointments.



You will assist with project coordination by tracking RFIs (Requests for Information), submittals, and project correspondence. You will update project logs, spreadsheets, and reporting dashboards while coordinating communication between architects, engineers, contractors, and other project stakeholders. You will monitor project updates and ensure records remain accurate and current.



You will also perform data entry and reporting tasks, generate basic project status reports, and assist with quality checks to ensure documentation is complete and properly formatted.



As part of BIM workflow support, you will assist BIM teams with the administrative aspects of BIM processes, maintain BIM-related records, and support model-sharing and collaboration workflows under the direction of BIM specialists.



Qualifications



Candidates should have previous experience as a Virtual Assistant, Administrative Assistant, Project Coordinator, or a similar support role. Strong organizational and time-management skills are essential, along with proficiency in Microsoft Office and Google Workspace. Excellent written and verbal communication skills are required, as well as the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously while maintaining a high level of accuracy and attention to detail.



Preference will be given to candidates who have familiarity with the Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry, experience using BIM 360, Autodesk Construction Cloud, Procore, or similar construction management platforms, and a basic understanding of construction drawings and project documentation.



Important Information



This position is a support role and is not responsible for BIM model creation, Revit modeling, clash detection, technical design coordination, or architectural and engineering decision-making. Those responsibilities remain with BIM Coordinators, BIM Specialists, Architects, and Engineers.



Employment Type



This is a remote position and may be offered on either a full-time or part-time basis depending on project requirements and business needs.

title: Senior MSP Engineer
description:
OVERVIEW 



The number one goal of everyone on our team is to deliver an exceptional service and experience to our clients. The Senior MSP Engineer (L3) plays a critical role in achieving that by serving as the highest technical escalation point in the service desk and resolving the issues no one else can. 



This is a senior, hands-on technical role. The L3 Engineer owns the most complex i
 and problems, leads root-cause analysis on recurring issues, and raises the technical bar for the entire team. 



Beyond firefighting, the L3 Engineer designs and improves client environments, contributes to standards and automation, and mentors L1 and L2 technicians so that fewer issues ever reach the top of the stack. 



This position requires deep, broad technical expertise across networking, identity, endpoint security, device management, and cloud, paired with the judgment to make sound decisions under pressure and the communication skills to lead during high-impact situations. 



RESPONSIBILITIES & TASKS 



TECHNICAL ESCALATION (PRIMARY FUNCTION) 

- Serve as the final escalation point for the service desk on complex and high-impact issues 

- Diagnose and resolve advanced problems across networking, identity, endpoint security, device management, and cloud 

- Lead root-cause analysis and permanent fixes for recurring or systemic issues 

- Own major i
 end to end, coordinating resources and communication until resolution

- Make sound technical decisions quickly during outages and high-pressure situations 



COMPLEX PROJECT & ARCHITECTURE WORK 

- Design and implement complex solutions across client environments 

- Lead the most technically demanding projects and migrations 

- Review and improve client architecture for reliability, performance, and security 

- Set and enforce technical standards and configuration baselines 



CUSTOMER EXPERIENCE

- Deliver a high-quality, professional, and consultative client experience 

- Communicate clearly with stakeholders during complex issues and changes 

- Act as a trusted senior technical advisor for clients and internal teams 

- Ensure minimal disruption to client operations during high-impact work 



USE OF TICKETING / PROJECT SYSTEMS 

- Accurately log all time, notes, and work performed in Pylon (ticketing system of record) 

- Track project deliverables and tasks in Linear 

- Capture root-cause findings and resolutions so they become reusable knowledge 

- Ensure all deliverables are properly recorded and transitioned 



TOOLS & PLATFORM EXPERTISE 

- Operate at an expert level across the MSSP toolstack, including: 

- Ticketing / PSA: Pylon (system of record), HaloPSA (contracts and billing) 

- Endpoint security: CrowdStrike with Flight Control (multi-tenant), ThreatLocker, Senteon 

- Identity: Okta, Beyond Identity, Keeper 

- Network: Cato Networks, FortiGate, Island Enterprise Browser 

- Device management: NinjaOne, Addigy, Intune, Apple Business Manager 

- Compliance / GRC: Vanta, Drata 

- Identify and drive improvements to tooling, standards, and automation 

- Partner with the Automation Engineer to eliminate recurring manual work 



COMMUNICATION, REPORTING & RISK MANAGEMENT 

- Identify and proactively communicate risks, blockers, or technical debt 

- Escalate business-level concerns to the Service Delivery Manager when needed 

- Provide clear status updates during major i
 and projects 

- Ensure alignment between technical execution and client expectations 



TEAMWORK & LEADERSHIP 

- Mentor and coach L1 and L2 technicians and engineers 

- Lead by example on quality, documentation, and client communication 

- Follow and contribute to Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) 

- Identify opportunities to improve processes, standardization, and delivery 

- Contribute to innovation and continuous improvement initiatives 



SKILLS AND ATTRIBUTES 



REQUIRED / DESIRED 

- Deep, broad experience resolving complex issues in an MSP or multi-client environment 

- Advanced networking expertise (firewalls, VLANs, routing, VPN, DNS, SASE/SD-WAN) 

- Advanced Microsoft 365 and identity experience (Entra ID, Intune, Exchange, Conditional Access)

- Hands-on experience with modern identity platforms (Okta, Beyond Identity, or similar) 

- Strong endpoint security experience (EDR, application control, hardening) 

- Multi-platform device management experience (Windows, macOS, mobile) 

- Solid understanding of compliance and GRC tooling (Vanta, Drata, or equivalent) 

- Scripting and automation experience (PowerShell preferred) 

- Excellent troubleshooting and root-cause analysis under pressure 

- Strong communication skills with technical and non-technical audiences 

- A deep desire to deliver an exceptional client experience 



NICE TO HAVE 

- Hands-on experience with tools in our stack (CrowdStrike, ThreatLocker, Okta, Beyond Identity, Cato Networks, NinjaOne, Addigy, Pylon) 

- Experience leading major i
 and complex migrations 

Certifications such as: 

- Microsoft role-based certs (e.g., AZ-104, AZ-305, MS-102) 

- Networking (CCNA or vendor-specific firewall certifications) 

- Identity / IAM certifications (Okta or similar) 

- ITIL / ITSM 

- Experience contributing to automation and standardization initiatives 

- Experience with, or a strong interest in, working on LLM-based (Large Language Model) projects, including evaluating, implementing, or integrating AI-driven solutions such as automation workflows, data analysis, knowledge retrieval, and conversational systems into business or technical environments. 



KEY DIFFERENTIATOR FROM JUNIOR ROLES 

Owns the hardest problems instead of escalating them 

Fixes root causes, not just symptoms 

Raises the technical capability of the entire team

Operates as a technical leader and final line of defense, not a ticket processor

title: Loan Processor / Lending Operations Coordinator
description:
We are a U.S.-based private money lending company that provides short-term, asset-based loans to real estate investors. We focus on first- and second-position loans, bridge funding, gap funding, and creative real estate transactions.

We value clean execution, capital protection, and professional communication.



Role Overview

We are hiring a Loan Processor / Lending Operations Coordinator to run borrower intake, manage our loan pipeline, and prepare deal files for underwriting. This role is the operational backbone of our lending business and works directly with borrowers, brokers, and internal leadership.



This is not a bank mortgage role. You will support private money and creative real estate deals using a CRM pipeline (GoHighLevel) and documented internal SOPs.



Key Responsibilities



Borrower Intake & Pipeline Management

Respond to new borrower applications and CRM inquiries the same business day

Send first-touch outreach to all new borrower leads promptly

Follow up consistently to collect missing application items

Accurately track and update borrower status through the correct CRM pipeline stages

Keep the pipeline clean — no stale files, no unanswered leads

Flag urgent or high-priority deals for leadership without delay





Loan File Organization & Documentation

Create and maintain borrower folders in Google Drive per company naming conventions

Collect ALL required documents before escalating a file: purchase agreement, rehab budget/scope of work, ARV comps, property photos, borrower ID, LLC documents (Operating Agreement + proof of good standing), verified HUDs, insurance, and a clearly stated exit strategy

Track all documents and file status accurately in the CRM

Submit complete, clearly labeled files that are ready for underwriting





SOP Adherence & Deal Pre-Qualification

Pre-qualify deals against our lending criteria before escalating (private money vs. hard money vs. hybrid)

Apply our quick-screen criteria accurately (LTV, borrower spread, combined leverage, close timeline)

Verify all non-negotiable borrower requirements

Route deals that fall outside our criteria to our referral process per SOP

Escalate unclear or borderline deals to leadership — never force a file through



Communication & Reporting



Provide consistent daily end-of-day (EOD) updates: completed, pending, needs attention

Communicate professionally and clearly with borrowers throughout the loan process

Proactively surface open loops, urgent items, and potential issues without being asked

Log all borrower conversations and decisions in the CRM accurately and promptly



Important Authority Boundaries



You will prepare, organize, and pre-qualify deals — but you will not approve loans, set terms, or make funding decisions. All approvals and final decisions stay with internal leadership.

Requirements



2+ years experience in real estate transactions, loan processing, or lending support

Strong attention to detail and organization

Excellent written and spoken English

Comfortable communicating with U.S.-based clients

Ability to manage multiple deals at once without dropping follow-ups

Experience using CRMs and pipeline-based systems

Reliable daily availability and consistent EOD reporting



Nice to Have (Not Required)



Private money, hard money, or creative real estate (subject-to, seller finance) experience

Familiarity with real estate investing terminology and underwriting basics (ARV, LTV, HUDs, exit strategy)

Experience pulling comps (e.g., PropStream, Redfin)

GoHighLevel or similar CRM experience



What Success Looks Like



Clean, accurate CRM records with every lead answered

Deals move smoothly with minimal rework

Files reach leadership complete and ready for underwriting

Borrowers feel informed and supported

Leadership does not need to fix or chase files



Growth Path



Strong performers move into expanded responsibility: full pipeline management without daily supervision, loan-file audits, lead generation in investor communities, weekly pipeline and loan-admin reporting, and coordinating document requests with borrowers and title companies.



How to Apply



Please submit your resume along with a brief introduction explaining your relevant experience and why you're an excellent fit for this role. Include the word "Lending" in your application message so we know you read this fully.

title: Spanish Content QA Assistant – YouTube Script Production (Claude AI)
description:
IMPORTANT: This job requires advanced or native-level Castilian Spanish. This is non-negotiable. If you do not have a strong command of written Spanish from Spain, please do not apply.



---



WHAT THIS JOB IS



I run a Spanish-language YouTube channel focused on Stoic philosophy for sleep and mental wellness. I need a virtual assistant to help manage the production of long-form scripts using a fully systematized process powered by Claude AI.



This is NOT a writing or creative job. You will not be writing scripts. You will be operating a system. Everything you need is provided: 



A detailed onboarding document

Word files to attach to Claude

Exact prompts to copy and paste at each step

A quality checklist to follow when reviewing the output. 



Your job is to execute the process precisely and pay very close attention to the corrections that need to be requested from Claude, following the quality requirements exactly.



The key skill this job requires is not creativity or knowledge of the topic. It is the ability to follow a detailed system step by step, read carefully, and apply correction criteria with precision and consistency.



---



WHAT THE PROCESS LOOKS LIKE



Step 1 — You set up a Claude project using the documents and instructions we provide. This takes around 5 minutes and is fully explained in the onboarding document.



Step 2 — Using the exact prompts we give you, you generate the script lesson by lesson inside the Claude project. Claude does all the writing. Each script contains approximately 30,000 words generated automatically by Claude. Your role is not to write the content yourself. Instead, you will supervise the generation process, review each lesson using the provided quality checklist, and request corrections when needed. The writing itself is handled by Claude; your responsibility is quality control and ensuring that the output meets the standards defined in the system.



Step 3 — You review each lesson against a detailed quality checklist we provide. When something does not meet the criteria, you request specific corrections from Claude following the exact instructions we give you for each type of issue. The checklist tells you exactly what to look for and how to ask for changes.



Step 4 — You deliver the completed and reviewed script as a Word document.



Every single step is documented. You will never need to improvise or make creative decisions. What is required is careful attention, precision, and a genuine commitment to following the process correctly.



---



WHAT WE PROVIDE



- A complete onboarding document explaining every step of the process

- All Word documents to attach to the Claude project

- The exact prompts to use at each moment of the process

- A detailed quality checklist with specific criteria and instructions for every type of correction

- Full support during the first script to answer any questions (we strongly encourage asking questions at any point, especially during the first script — the sooner any doubt is raised, the faster the process becomes fully manageable and the easier it is to correct course before too much work has been done)



---



REQUIREMENTS



- Advanced or native Castilian Spanish. This is the most critical requirement. The channel uses only standard Spanish from Spain and you need to read and evaluate the text accurately.

- Access to Claude.ai Pro plan ($20/month). This is the tool used for all script generation. It is required to do this job.

- Strong attention to detail and ability to follow written instructions with precision.

- Reliable availability and consistent communication.



---



VOLUME AND SCOPE



We produce approximately 1 script every 2 days. Each script contains between 20 and 25 lessons and totals around 30,000 words — generated by Claude following the system, not written manually by you.



We will start with a paid trial of 1 complete script. If the process goes well and the quality meets the standards, the first project will consist of 10 scripts. The goal is to build a long-term working relationship with the right person.



---



TO APPLY





Please write your application in Spanish and tell us:



Your Spanish level and how you acquired it.



Your experience with AI tools — especially giving precise correction instructions to get specific results.



Can you spot typical AI writing patterns in Spanish text — repetitive structures, formulaic phrases, transitions that feel unnatural or interchangeable between paragraphs? If so, could you give us 3 or 4 concrete examples of the kind of constructions you would flag? This is one of the most important skills for this role.



Any experience following detailed checklists or quality control processes.



Applications in English only will not be considered.

title: WEB DEVELOPER — FULL-STACK SAAS + WEBSITE
description:
Build a College Counseling SaaS Platform + Branded Client Website

Multi-Tenant  •  White-Label  •  Stripe Billing  •  College Database  •  Financial Aid Engine

Remote  •  Project-Based 



Overview

We are building a new SaaS platform for independent college counselors — a direct competitor to CounselMore, CollegePlannerPro, and GuidedPath. The platform will give counselors a complete operating system: CRM, student and parent portals, task management, document storage, college database, academic fit scoring, and a financial aid planning engine.



This is not a website project.

We need a senior developer or technical lead who has built secure, multi-tenant SaaS applications with user roles, subscription billing, client portals, document storage, and scalable architecture. If you have only built websites or simple apps, this is not the right project for you.



Three Connected Products



Product 1SaaS Platform

The main build. A multi-tenant, subscription-based platform that any independent college counselor across the US can subscribe to monthly. Each counselor gets their own isolated workspace, branding, students, documents, and billing.

Product 2CCP Website

Rebuild 
 as a modern marketing and booking site. Connects to the SaaS platform via API so College Career Pathways clients experience a fully branded portal at 
. College Career Pathways is Subscriber #1.

Product 3Database + Aid Engine

Planned differentiator module (may follow MVP). Searchable US college database, academic fit scoring, parent financial profile, FAFSA/SAI estimator, per-school net cost breakdown, and scholarship matching engine.



URL Structure

Public website:       

Branded portal:      

SaaS platform:       app.[productname].com





Job Details

Position

Senior Full-Stack SaaS Developer / Technical Lead

Type

Project-based build + ongoing retainer after launch

Location

Remote 

Commitment

Full-time during build phase; part-time retainer after launch

Start Date

ASAP

Project Style

Paid discovery sprint first, then staged development milestones

Rate

Please include fixed-price proposal in your application





Important: No Zapier Dependency

Core product functionality must not depend on Zapier. Use direct APIs, webhooks, custom backend workflows, scheduled jobs, or native integrations.



Acceptable Approaches

    • Direct API integrations

    • Webhooks and event-driven backend workflows

    • Custom backend jobs and scheduled cron jobs

    • Self-hostable workflow automation tools — your recommendation

    • Native app integrations built directly into the platform





Recommended Tech Stack & Third-Party Resources

We have done significant research into available tools and data sources. The lists below are our starting recommendations. The developer's job is to evaluate what is actually integrable, determine licensing terms and costs, and propose the best combination — prioritizing free or low-cost options wherever possible. Your Phase 0 deliverables must include a final vendor/tool recommendation with justification and estimated cost for each layer.



Core Platform Stack

Frontend

Next.js / React (strongly preferred). Webflow acceptable for the CCP marketing site only.

Backend / Database

PostgreSQL — required. Supabase (preferred), Neon, PlanetScale, or managed Postgres on 
.

Authentication

Supabase Auth (free tier generous) or Clerk (generous free tier, excellent multi-tenant support). Must support MFA, role-based access, and session management.

Tenant Isolation

PostgreSQL row-level security (RLS) — preferred. Alternative: separate schemas per tenant. Justify your approach.

File Storage

Supabase Storage (free tier included), AWS S3 (pay-per-use), or Cloudflare R2 (very low cost, S3-compatible). Google Drive API integration required for all user types — see Google Integration section below.

Payments

Stripe — non-negotiable. Subscriptions, webhooks, Stripe Customer Portal, plan limits, seat-based pricing.

Hosting

Vercel (frontend, generous free tier), Render, Railway, or 
. AWS if scale requires it.


Resend (generous free tier, developer-friendly), Postmark, or SendGrid. For transactional notifications, invitations, and reminders.

Scheduling


 (open source, self-hostable, free) or Calendly (paid). 
 preferred for cost.

Workflow / Jobs

n8n (open source, self-hostable), 
v (open source), Inngest, or Pipedream. NO Zapier dependency.

CMS


 (generous free tier) or Contentful — for blog/resources pages on the CCP website if needed.

Error Monitoring

Sentry (generous free tier for small teams). Required for production SaaS.

Analytics

PostHog (open source, generous free cloud tier) or Plausible. For platform usage analytics.

Admin Tools

Retool (free for small teams), Appsmith (open source), or custom-built admin dashboard in Next.js.

Mobile / Browser

No native app. Full functionality on mobile browser (iOS Safari, Android Chrome). Mobile-first design required.

Search UI

Next.js server-side filtering against local Supabase/Postgres database. Algolia or Typesense if full-text search performance requires it.



College Data Sources

The following are known US government and institutional data sources for college information. Most are free. The developer should evaluate each for completeness, update frequency, and integration complexity, and recommend the best combination.



College Scorecard 
/data/documentation

Free. US Dept of Education. 6,700+ institutions. Covers: tuition, net price by income bracket, acceptance rate, SAT/ACT ranges, graduation rate, retention rate, median earnings, debt, programs/majors, enrollment. Updated annually. REST API and bulk CSV download available. Primary recommended source.

IPEDS — Integrated PostsecondaryEducation Data 
/ipeds

Free. National Center for Education Statistics. Extremely comprehensive — the federal standard for institutional data. Bulk data downloads by year. Covers: enrollment, completions, graduation rates, finances, staff, tuition, aid. Use to supplement College Scorecard.

College 
/collegenavigator

Free. NCES consumer-facing tool powered by IPEDS data. Useful reference for data fields and coverage.

Common Data Set (CDS)

Free. Voluntarily published by most colleges annually. Best source for average GPA, class rank policies, and detailed admissions data not always in federal datasets. Not available via API — requires scraping or manual curation per institution.

Peterson's 

Commercial. Comprehensive college profiles including GPA data, test policies, financial aid. Licensed data feed — evaluate cost vs. benefit.


 

Partially free. Student reviews and rankings. Not a primary data source but useful supplemental context.

College Board 

Free consumer tool. College Board data. Evaluate for API access or data partnership options.

US News College Data

Commercial. Rankings and profile data. Licensed — evaluate cost.



Developer note: Average GPA is not consistently available in federal datasets. The Common Data Set is the best source but requires manual curation or scraping. The platform must allow GPA fields to be labeled by source: official, Common Data Set, manually curated, counselor estimate, or unknown. Evaluate whether a curated GPA dataset can be licensed from Peterson's or built manually for the top 1,000–2,000 schools.



Financial Aid Data & Calculation Resources

The following are known resources for implementing the financial aid estimation engine. The developer should evaluate each and propose a specific implementation approach in Phase 0.



Federal Student AidEstimator 
/aid-estimator

Free. The US Dept of Education publishes the Student Aid Index (SAI) formula publicly. The developer can implement this formula directly in the backend — no API required. The formula is updated annually and is publicly documented.

FAFSA Simplification ActFormula (post-2024)

Free. The SAI formula changed significantly starting with the
aid year under the FAFSA Simplification Act. The developer must use the current formula, not the old EFC formula. Documentation available at 
.

College Scorecard Net Priceby Income 

Free. Already in the College Scorecard API. Provides historical average net price broken into income brackets per institution. Use for estimated net cost per school — not a guarantee of individual aid.

IPEDS Student FinancialAid 
/ipeds

Free. Institutional financial aid data including average aid awarded, percent receiving aid, and average net price. Use to supplement Scorecard data.

CSS Profile School 
/css-profile/about/college-list

Free. College Board publishes a list of schools that require the CSS Profile for institutional aid. The platform should flag these schools in the college list and financial aid module.

Net Price CalculatorLinks per School

Free. Every federally funded institution is required by law to publish a net price calculator. College Scorecard includes NPC URLs for most schools. The platform should link to each school's official NPC.



Free reference resource. Comprehensive financial aid information, formulas, and calculators. Useful for developer research but not an API source.

National Association ofStudent Financial AidAdministrators (NASFAA)

Free reference resource. Industry standards and policy updates for financial aid. Useful for developer research.



Scholarship Data Sources

The following are known scholarship databases and APIs. The developer should research licensing terms, API availability, and cost for each, and propose the best approach for the MVP rules engine.




 

Scholarship database and platform. Evaluate for API access and data licensing terms. Targets students directly but may offer institutional/partner access.

Scholarship 

Scholarship matching platform. Evaluate for API or data partnership access.



One of the largest free scholarship databases. Owned by Monster. Evaluate for data partnership or API access.



Scholarship and college search platform. Evaluate for data access or partnership.

Niche 
/colleges/scholarships

Free scholarship listings on 
. Evaluate for scraping or data partnership.

Chegg 
/scholarships

Large scholarship database. Evaluate for API or licensing access.

Going 

Scholarship platform focused on counselor workflows. Evaluate for partnership or data access — may be most relevant given our use case.

College-Specific Merit Aid(manually curated)

Many colleges publish automatic merit scholarship criteria based on GPA and test scores publicly on their admissions websites. For top 500-1,000 schools, these can be manually curated into the scholarship rules engine without any API dependency. Recommend starting here for MVP.

Federal Pell Grant(
)

Free. Pell Grant eligibility is determined by the SAI formula already implemented in the financial aid engine. No separate data source needed — flag automatically when SAI qualifies.

State Grant Programs

Each US state has its own grant programs with varying eligibility rules. Consider building a manually curated state grant table for the 50 states as a Phase 3 addition.



Scheduling & Calendar Integration

For session booking on the College Career Pathways website and optionally within the counselor dashboard.









Widely used. Free tier available but limited. Paid plans start at ~$10/month per user. Embeddable widget and API available.





Google Calendar 
/calendar

Free. If building a native scheduling system, Google Calendar API can be used for availability sync and event creation. More complex to implement but no per-user cost.



Google Workspace Integration — Required

Google Drive and Google Docs integration is a hard requirement for all user types.

Students, parents, and counselors already live and work in Google Workspace. The platform must connect natively to Google Drive and Google Docs so users can link, upload, view, and collaborate on documents without leaving their existing workflow. This is not optional — it applies to all user roles.



Google Drive 
/drive

Free (within Google API quota limits). Allows the platform to browse, read, upload, and link files in a user's Google Drive. Must be available to counselors, students, and parents.

Google Docs 
/docs

Free (within quota). Allows the platform to read, create, and embed Google Docs — critical for essay drafting, collaborative editing, and counselor feedback on student writing.

Google Picker 
/drive/api/guides/picker

Free. Google's native file picker UI — allows users to select files directly from their own Google Drive without granting full Drive access. Clean and secure integration pattern.

Google OAuth 2.
/identity

Free. Required for authenticating users with their Google account and requesting Drive/Docs permissions scoped to what the platform needs.

Google Calendar 
/calendar

Free. Sync counselor availability and session appointments to Google Calendar. Relevant for scheduling integration.



Required Google Integration Features by User Role



All Users — Counselors, Students, Parents

    • Connect Google account via OAuth — one-time authorization per user

    • Browse and select files from their own Google Drive using Google Picker

    • Attach Google Drive files to their profile, tasks, or document sections in the platform

    • View linked Google Docs directly within the platform (embedded or linked)

    • Files linked from Google Drive do not need to be re-uploaded — the platform stores the Drive link and displays a preview or direct link



Counselors

    • Create and share Google Docs directly with students from within the platform

    • Attach counselor-created Google Docs (feedback letters, notes, resources) to a student's record

    • Upload files from Google Drive to the platform's secure document storage where appropriate

    • Share Google Drive folders or files with individual students/parents from within the platform

    • Sync session appointments to Google Calendar



Students

    • Submit essays, personal statements, and supplements by linking Google Docs — no need to download and re-upload

    • Receive counselor feedback directly on Google Docs via comments

    • Upload transcripts, test scores, and other documents from Google Drive

    • View counselor-shared Google Docs and resources in the portal



Parents

    • Upload financial documents and forms from Google Drive

    • View documents and resources shared by counselor through Google Drive links

    • Attach financial aid forms, tax documents, or other files via Google Drive picker



Architecture note: 

Google Drive links should be stored as references in the platform database — not necessarily copied into the platform's own storage. This avoids duplication and keeps files in the user's own Google account where they control them.

For sensitive documents (transcripts, financial forms) that need to be in platform-controlled storage with access controls and audit logging, the platform should support both — import from Drive into platform storage OR store as a Drive link with permission checking.





Phase 0 — Paid Discovery & Architecture Sprint

Before full development begins, we want a paid discovery and planning sprint. The goal is to make sure the product is architected correctly before a single line of production code is written.



Please include your proposed cost and timeline for Phase 0 in your application.



Phase 0 Deliverables

    • Product requirements document

    • User stories

    • MVP scope with feature prioritization — what to build first vs. later

    • Technical architecture document

    • Database schema and multi-tenant data model

    • Role and permission model

    • API design

    • Stripe billing plan

    • Security approach

    • Wireframes or clickable prototype

    • Development roadmap with milestones

    • Timeline and budget estimate by phase





Product 1 — SaaS Platform Scope

1. Multi-Tenancy

Each subscribing counselor or counseling practice gets a completely isolated workspace. No counselor should ever be able to see another counselor's data. Every major table and record must be scoped by tenant.



Per-Tenant Features

    • Separate workspace, branding, students, parents, documents, tasks, college lists, financial data, and billing

    • Counselor signs up and subscribes via Stripe — gets admin dashboard

    • Counselor invites students and parents to their branded portal

    • Tenant-specific branding — logo, colors, portal subdomain (e.g., 
)

    • Optional custom domain support

    • Option to hide SaaS product branding on higher-tier plans

    • Tenant-specific portal settings and usage limits

    • Super-admin can view and manage all tenants



2. User Roles & Permissions



Platform Owner / Super Admin

Manages all tenants, billing, support access, system settings, usage metrics, and platform-wide configuration. Impersonation/support mode.

Counseling Business Owner

Full access within their own tenant — students, parents, counselors/staff, billing, branding, templates, settings.

Counselor / Staff

Access to assigned students — tasks, documents, notes, messages, application trackers, college lists.

Student

Own dashboard only — assigned tasks, uploaded documents, college list, application tracker, essay tracker, resources, counselor updates.

Parent / Guardian

Linked student overview, parent-visible tasks, financial aid forms, documents, meeting summaries, counselor updates, billing/payment links.

Read-Only Parent / Guardian

Limited view-only access for divorced/separated families or restricted situations. Cannot upload or interact.



Important: Student users must not automatically see parent financial data. Financial profile data is restricted to counselor and parent roles only.



3. Counselor Dashboard

    • Student roster — add, manage, archive student profiles

    • Parent/guardian records — link multiple parents to one student, sibling/family linking

    • Student academic profile — weighted/unweighted GPA, SAT, ACT, class rank, AP/IB/dual credit, intended major

    • Counseling status and pipeline tracking

    • Tags, internal notes, assigned counselor, contact history

    • Task management — assign, track, view overdue tasks across all students

    • Document management — upload, organize, set visibility

    • Application tracker and college list tracker

    • Meeting/session notes and internal counselor notes

    • Resource sharing with students and parents — share Google Drive files and Docs directly from within the platform

    • Google Drive integration — browse, attach, and share files from Google Drive without leaving the platform

    • Google Calendar sync — counselor availability and session appointments synced to Google Calendar

    • Create and share Google Docs with individual students for essay feedback and collaborative notes

    • Search and filter across student roster

    • Upcoming deadline view and overdue task view



4. Student & Parent Portal

Student Portal

    • Branded login — counselor logo and colors, not SaaS platform branding

    • Dashboard — assigned tasks, upcoming deadlines, notifications

    • Document uploads — directly from device or from Google Drive via Google Picker

    • Submit essays and personal statements by linking a Google Doc — no download/re-upload required

    • View counselor feedback and comments directly in linked Google Docs

    • View transcripts, test scores, and other documents shared by counselor

    • College list and application tracker

    • Essay tracker — link Google Docs per essay, track word count, deadline, and submission status

    • Resource library — view and open counselor-shared Google Docs and Drive files

    • Meeting notes and next steps from counselor



Parent Portal

    • Linked student overview and upcoming deadlines

    • Parent-visible tasks

    • Upload financial documents from device or Google Drive

    • View documents and resources shared by counselor via Google Drive links

    • Meeting summaries and counselor updates

    • Billing/payment links where applicable

    • Resource library

    • Financial profile input — if granted access (see Product 3)



Mobile browser requirement — no app required.

Students, parents, and counselors must be able to use the full portal on a mobile phone browser (iOS Safari, Android Chrome) without downloading any app. This is not just responsive CSS — it means touch-friendly navigation, fast load times, readable layouts on small screens, tap-sized buttons, and forms that work correctly on mobile keyboards. Design mobile-first, not mobile-adapted.



5. Task & Checklist System

    • Task templates and custom tasks

    • Grade-based checklists — 9th, 10th, 11th, 12th grade tracks

    • Student-specific and parent-specific tasks

    • Due dates, status tracking, recurring items

    • Overdue reminders and notifications

    • Counselor view of all pending and overdue tasks across student roster



Example Tasks

    • Upload transcript and test scores

    • Complete activity list and resume

    • Draft personal statement

    • Request recommendation letters

    • Complete FAFSA and CSS Profile

    • Run net price calculator

    • Submit college application by deadline

    • Upload scholarship application materials



6. Secure Document Management

    • Upload by counselor, student, or parent — directly from device or from Google Drive

    • Link Google Drive files without re-uploading — platform stores the Drive reference

    • Import from Google Drive into platform storage for sensitive documents requiring access control and audit logging

    • Files organized by student

    • Visibility controls — counselor-only, parent-visible, student-visible

    • Secure storage via Supabase Storage, AWS S3, or equivalent for platform-hosted files

    • Google Drive links stored as references with permission checking where appropriate

    • Audit logs and activity logs — all uploads, downloads, deletions, and link accesses

    • Download controls and access-controlled download URLs

    • Tenant-level file separation



Google Docs for essays: Students should be able to submit essays and personal statements by linking a Google Doc. Counselors can then comment directly in the Google Doc and the student sees feedback in their existing workflow. The platform tracks the Doc link, submission status, and version — without requiring a separate file upload.



Security is critical. The platform will store sensitive student records, family financial information, and confidential documents. Files imported into platform storage must be encrypted, access-controlled, and audit-logged. Google Drive links must verify that the sharing permissions are appropriate before displaying to any user.



7. College List & Application Tracker

College Categories

    • Reach / Target / Likely / Financial Safety / Merit-Aid Target

    • Removed / Not Pursuing



Application Types

8. Messaging & Updates

MVP Version

Future Version

 threading

9. Subscription & Billing

Stripe Billing for all SaaS subscriptions. For MVP, a single flat monthly plan is acceptable if the architecture can support additional plans and seat-based pricing later.



Billing Requirements

11. Data Import & Migration

Leah's practice is currently using CounselMore with live students, parents, documents, and data. Future subscribers will also arrive with existing data in spreadsheets or other tools. Migration support must be in the architecture from day one, even if not fully built in Phase 1.

    • Architecture must support future migration from CounselMore or similar platforms

12. Public SaaS Marketing Site

A simple marketing site to sell subscriptions to other counselors. Separate from the College Career Pathways website.



    • Home / Features / Pricing / Demo / FAQ / Contact / Login / Sign Up

    • Free trial CTA

    • Designed to attract independent college counselors as subscribers





Product 2 — College Career Pathways Website

Rebuild 
 as a fast, modern, SEO-optimized marketing and booking website for our own college counseling practice. This is Product 1's first real customer.



Pages

    • Home

    • Services & Pricing

    • About (Leah / College Career Pathways story)

    • Resources

    • Contact and inquiry forms

    • Book a Session — Calendly integration

    • Client Login — authenticates against SaaS platform, routes to branded portal

    • Blog/resources section if recommended



API Integration Requirements

    • Client login on CCP site authenticates against the SaaS platform via API

    • Students and parents land in a branded portal at 

    • Experience is fully branded to College Career Pathways — no SaaS platform branding visible

    • All data (tasks, documents, progress, college list, financials) served from SaaS platform

    • Stripe payment integration for session booking fees

    •
 notification integration



The CCP website is the front door. The SaaS platform is the engine behind it. Clients should not see the seam.





Product 3 — College Database & Financial Aid Engine

This is a planned differentiator module that may be built after the core SaaS MVP, depending on timeline and budget. It is what separates this platform from every competitor in the space.



Part A — Searchable College Database

Recommended Data Sources

The following sources have been identified. The developer should evaluate each for integration complexity, data completeness, and licensing terms, and propose the best combination. Most are free federal datasets.



    • College Scorecard API / bulk data (
) — Free. Primary recommended source. REST API and CSV bulk download. Covers tuition, net price by income bracket, SAT/ACT ranges, acceptance rate, graduation rate, outcomes, programs, enrollment.

    • IPEDS / NCES bulk data (
/ipeds) — Free. The federal standard. Comprehensive annual data downloads. Use to supplement College Scorecard with fields it does not cover.

    • College Navigator (
/collegenavigator) — Free. Consumer-facing NCES tool. Useful reference for field mapping.

    • Common Data Set (
) — Free. Best available source for average GPA and detailed admissions data. Not available via API — evaluate manual curation or scraping for top institutions.

    • Peterson's (
) — Commercial. Most comprehensive GPA coverage. Evaluate licensing cost vs. benefit.



Developer note: Average GPA is not consistently in federal datasets. The Common Data Set is the best free source but requires manual curation. The platform must allow GPA fields labeled by source: official, Common Data Set, manually curated, counselor estimate, or unknown. Propose a solution for GPA coverage in Phase 0.



All college data must be stored locally and refreshed periodically — do not query live during user searches. Each data point must include source, data year, and last updated.



    • Financial aid indicators and net price calculator links

    • Graduation rate, retention rate, average debt, post-graduation earnings

    • Majors and programs offered

    • Scholarship and financial aid URLs

Data must be stored locally and refreshed periodically — not queried live during user searches. Each data point must include source, data year, and last updated.



Search & Filter Fields

    • College name, city, state, region, distance from student home ZIP

    • Public / private / non-profit / for-profit / 2-year / 4-year

    • Campus setting — urban, suburban, rural

    • Undergraduate enrollment size

    • Acceptance rate

    • SAT / ACT 25th–75th percentile ranges

    • Average GPA where available (labeled by source)

    • Test-optional / test-required status where available

    • Majors and programs offered

    • In-state and out-of-state tuition and fees

    • Total Cost of Attendance (COA)

    • Average net price — overall and by income bracket where available

    • Graduation rate and retention rate

    • Average debt at graduation

    • Median earnings and post-graduation outcomes

    • Financial aid generosity indicators

    • Net price calculator link and financial aid URL

    • Scholarship URL if available

    • Keyword search



College Profile Pages

    • All data fields above displayed clearly, each showing source, data year, and last updated

    • Estimated net cost for this family — pulled live from financial profile if entered (Part B)

    • 'Add to My List' — one click adds the school to the student's application tracker

    • Reach / Target / Likely tag — auto-suggested based on academic fit, counselor-editable

    • Counselor notes field per school per student



Part B — Parent Financial Profile

Stored securely per student. Accessible by counselor and parent roles only — student login must not see financial data.



Financial Intake Fields

    • Parent marital status

    • Household size and number of children in college simultaneously

    • State of residence

    • Parent AGI (Adjusted Gross Income)

    • Parent assets — savings, checking, investments (excluding retirement accounts)

    • 529 plan assets

    • Business or farm ownership if applicable

    • Home equity — optional, used for institutional aid estimates at CSS Profile schools

    • Divorced / separated parent information

    • Non-custodial parent considerations

    • Student income and assets

    • Special circumstances notes



Part C — Financial Aid & Scholarship Estimator

Recommended Data Sources & Resources

The following are identified resources for implementing the financial aid estimation engine. Most are free. The developer should evaluate each and propose a specific implementation approach in Phase 0.



    • Federal SAI Formula (
/aid-estimator) — Free. The Student Aid Index formula is publicly documented by the US Dept of Education and can be implemented directly in the backend — no API required. Updated annually.

    • FAFSA Simplification Act Formula (
) — Free. The SAI formula changed significantly starting
. Developer must use the current post-simplification formula, not the old EFC formula.

    • College Scorecard Net Price by Income Bracket — Free. Already in the Scorecard dataset. Provides historical average net price per income bracket per institution. Use for estimated net cost per school.

    • IPEDS Student Financial Aid Data (
/ipeds) — Free. Average aid awarded, percent of students receiving aid, average net price. Supplement to Scorecard.

    • CSS Profile School List (
/css-profile) — Free. College Board publishes the list of schools requiring the CSS Profile for institutional aid. Flag these schools in the platform.

    • 
 (
) — Free reference resource. Comprehensive financial aid formulas and methodology. Useful for developer research.

    • NASFAA (
) — Free reference resource. Industry standard financial aid policy and formula updates.



Required Outputs

Whatever implementation approach is used, the financial aid module must produce:

    • Estimated SAI based on family financial inputs using current federal formula

    • Estimated federal grant eligibility (Pell) — auto-flagged when SAI qualifies

    • Estimated federal loan eligibility — subsidized and unsubsidized

    • Work-study planning indicators

    • CSS Profile flag for schools that require institutional aid forms

    • Per-school estimated net cost using available Scorecard/IPEDS net price data, income bracket data, federal aid estimates, and counselor-adjustable assumptions

    • Side-by-side affordability comparison table across all schools on the student's list

    • Financial Safety classification based on estimated net cost vs. family budget

    • Official net price calculator links per school

    • Ability to upload and save official NPC results per school

    • Scholarship matching against rules engine — award amounts, deadlines, application links

    • Counselor can mark scholarships as: Recommended / Applied / Awarded

    • Aid and scholarship deadline tracking



All outputs must be clearly labeled as estimates. The implementation must be accurate enough to be useful for planning without overstating precision.



Part D — Scholarship Rules Engine

Store scholarship criteria and match against student profiles. The following scholarship data sources have been identified for the developer to evaluate. MVP should start with a manually curated rules engine. Evaluate third-party API options for post-MVP enrichment.



Identified Scholarship Data Sources

    • 
 (
) — Scholarship platform. Evaluate for API access and data licensing terms.

    • Scholarship Owl (
) — Scholarship matching platform. Evaluate for API or data partnership.

    • Fastweb (
) — One of the largest free scholarship databases. Evaluate for data partnership or API access.

    • Going Merry (
) — Scholarship platform built specifically for counselor workflows. Most relevant to this use case — evaluate for partnership or data access.

    • Cappex (
) — Scholarship and college search platform. Evaluate for data access.

    • Niche Scholarships (
/colleges/scholarships) — Free listings. Evaluate for scraping or data partnership.

    • College-specific merit aid (manually curated) — Most colleges publish automatic merit scholarship criteria on their admissions websites based on GPA and test scores. For the top 500-1,000 schools, these can be entered manually into the rules engine for MVP. Recommend starting here.

    • Federal Pell Grant — No separate source needed. Pell eligibility is output directly from the SAI formula already implemented in Part C.

    • State grant programs — Each US state has its own grant programs. Consider building a manually curated state grant table as a Phase 3 addition.



Scholarship Rule Fields

    • College, scholarship name, award amount, renewable or one-time

    • Minimum GPA, minimum SAT, minimum ACT

    • Residency requirement, major requirement

    • Application required (yes/no), deadline, source URL

    • Confidence level and notes



The system must clearly distinguish between:

    • Automatic / guaranteed published awards

    • Competitive awards

    • Holistic awards

    • Counselor-entered scholarship notes

    • Third-party / private scholarships



Required Disclaimer (must appear persistently on all financial output screens):

"These figures are estimates only, based on publicly available data and the financial information provided. Actual financial aid awards, scholarships, grants, loans, and net price are determined by each institution and applicable federal/state aid rules after submission of required forms such as the FAFSA, CSS Profile, and institutional aid applications. This tool does not provide financial, legal, or tax advice."





Security & Privacy Requirements

The platform will store sensitive student records, family financial documents, and confidential information. Security must be treated seriously throughout — not bolted on later.



    • HTTPS / TLS encryption in transit

    • Encryption at rest where appropriate

    • Secure authentication with MFA support

    • Role-based access control with tenant-level data isolation

    • Secure file storage with access-controlled download URLs

    • Audit logs — must capture the following events specifically:

    • User logins and failed login attempts

    • Document uploads, downloads, and deletions

    • Financial profile views and edits

    • Task completions and status changes

    • Permission and role changes

    • Billing events — upgrades, cancellations, failed payments

    • Admin impersonation and support access events

    • Automated backups

    • User invitation flow and password reset

    • Data export and data deletion — GDPR/CCPA-ready

    • Privacy policy and Terms of Service support

    • Financial estimate disclaimer on all relevant screens



Please describe your recommended security approach in your application.





Deliverables by Phase

Phase 0 — Discovery & Architecture

    • Product requirements document and user stories

    • MVP scope with prioritization — build now vs. later

    • Technical architecture document

    • Security approach

Phase 1A — Core SaaS Foundation

The non-negotiable infrastructure. Nothing else can be built without this.



    • Multi-tenant backend with data isolation (RLS or equivalent)

    • User authentication and role-based access control

    • Google OAuth integration — all user types can connect their Google account

    • Counselor admin dashboard — student records, parent records, CRM basics

    • Task and checklist module

    • Super-admin panel
